assertion_results.text: The query-scope analysis identifies that the task targets a subset — specifically 'SPDX SBOMs' not all SBOMs — by extracting subset-indicating language from the Description section
assertion_results.evidence: query-scope.md lines 5-8 quote the task description targeting 'SPDX SBOMs'. Lines 10 state 'Target scope: SPDX SBOM documents only -- a subset of all SBOM documents in the system.' Lines 14-19 extract three subset-restricting phrases: '"all SPDX SBOMs" -- type qualifier limiting to SPDX documents', '"Only SPDX SBOMs need re-processing" -- explicit exclusion of other types', '"CycloneDX documents already have supplier information" -- states CycloneDX is out of scope'.

assertion_results.text: The query-scope analysis verifies that the sbom entity's labels column (jsonb) supports filtering by document type at the database level, rather than requiring application-level filtering
assertion_results.evidence: query-scope.md lines 22-29 under 'Available Database Filter': 'The `sbom` entity (`entity/src/sbom.rs`) has a `labels` column of type `jsonb` that stores document metadata. Per the Implementation Notes: SPDX documents have {"type": "spdx"} in their labels; CycloneDX documents have {"type": "cyclonedx"} in their labels. This means the subset restriction can be expressed at the query level using a jsonb field extraction filter'. Lines 81-87 under 'Correctness of Database-Level Filtering' further confirm: 'The `labels` jsonb column on the `sbom` entity is the authoritative source for document type classification... PostgreSQL's jsonb operator ->>"type" efficiently extracts the type field for filtering'.

assertion_results.text: The plan uses a filtered query to select only SPDX documents (e.g., WHERE labels->>'type' = 'spdx' or equivalent ORM filter) instead of loading all documents and discarding CycloneDX ones in application code
assertion_results.evidence: plan.md lines 53-58 show the ORM code: `sbom::Entity::find().filter(Expr::cust("labels->>'type' = 'spdx'")).all(db).await?;`. Lines 122-129 under 'Database Query Strategy' show the equivalent SQL: `SELECT * FROM sbom WHERE labels->>'type' = 'spdx'` and explain 'Filtering at the database level ensures only the relevant subset is loaded'. The code comments at lines 48-52 explicitly state 'CRITICAL: Do NOT use Sbom::find() or an unfiltered query'.

assertion_results.text: The plan or query-scope analysis explicitly mentions the performance impact of loading all documents — referencing that production environments have hundreds of thousands of non-target CycloneDX records
assertion_results.evidence: query-scope.md lines 58-59: 'The Implementation Notes explicitly state: "Production environments have hundreds of thousands of CycloneDX documents alongside a smaller number of SPDX documents."' Lines 61-78 detail impacts: 'Load hundreds of thousands of unnecessary records into memory', 'Trigger unnecessary I/O', 'Risk migration timeout or OOM'. plan.md lines 94-99: 'production environments have hundreds of thousands of CycloneDX records. An unfiltered Sbom::find() or Document::all() would load all records into memory, causing severe performance degradation: unnecessary disk I/O reading hundreds of thousands of CycloneDX source documents'.

assertion_results.text: The plan does NOT propose using an unfiltered query like Sbom::find() or Document::all() followed by an application-level type check to discard CycloneDX documents

Lines 48-52 comment: 'CRITICAL: Do NOT use Sbom::find() or an unfiltered query.' Lines 93-99 explicitly reject the unfiltered approach. query-scope.md summary table at line 96: 'Rejected approach: Sbom::find() / Document::all() + application-level filtering'.
